HYPERTENSION IN THE ED 
 
 
 
 
 
Hypertensive Emergency 
Elevated blood pressure with life-threatening acute 
end organ damage 
• Hypertensive encephalopathy & 
retinopathy 
• Haemorrhagic / Ischaemic CVA 
• ACS – STEMI/NSTE-ACS 
• Acute LV dysfunction / Congestive heart 
failure 
• Acute pulmonary oedema 
• Aortic dissection 
• Acute renal failure 
• Eclampsia / Pre-eclampsia 
 
 
Management of Hypertensive Emergencies 
• ABC approach to resuscitation 
• A – definitive airway if a depressed level of consciousness  
• B – Acute pulmonary oedema, but intubation is not indicated, start non-invasive 
ventilation (see NIV protocol) 
• C – Fluid bolus with Balsol / Ringers Lactate @ 10ml/kg prior to commencing IV anti-
hypertensive agent 
 
TREATMENT GOAL 
Within 1st hour: Reduce MAP by 20-25% only; DBP not less than 110mmHg except 
 Aortic Dissection:  Goal systolic < 100-120 within 20 minutes if tolerated 
 
 
Hypertensive Urgency 
Elevated blood pressure with signs of TOD but 
no immediate life-threatening complications 
• Severe headache 
• Blurred vision 
• Proteinuria 
• Mild LV failure 
 
Management 
§ Examination 
§ ECG 
§ Refer to cardiology – start oral 
antihypertensive agents aiming to 
decrease the BP over the next 2-3 days 
 
Nitroglycerin  
Indications  
• Acute pulmonary oedema 
• Acute LV dysfunction 
• ACS – STEMI/NSTE-ACS 
 
Nitroglycerin (Nitrocine®) Infusion (50μg/ml) 
• 10mg in 200ml Normal Saline 
• Withdraw 10mls Normal Saline before 
adding the Nitrocine® 
• Start at 12mls/hr (10μg/min) 
• Double the dose every 2 minutes until 
target BP is reached 
• Maximum 200 μg/min 
	
Labetalol  
Indications  
• Aortic dissection 
• Encephalopathy (confusion/seizures/coma) 
• CVA – haemorrhagic / ischaemic 
 
Labetalol (Trandate®)  
Bolus 
• 20 mg (4mls) then 
Infusion 
• Add 16 mls (80 mg) + a 2nd vial (100 mg) of 
Labetalol to 200 mls 0.9% Normal Saline 
(0.76 mg/ml) 
• Start infusion via infusion pump or dial-a-
flow at 80 ml/hr 
• Increase by 10 ml/hr every 5 minutes until 
BP target reached 
• Maximum 160 ml/hr (2 mg/min) 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020
